about: The ten fixed descriptions of diagrams that every large model is asked to write as a script for the editor (specification 18.3, Table 13 row 'Large model as author'). Written for this repository; one legend (legend_prompt.md) for all of them.

descriptions.text: The architecture of a small web shop: customers use a web client that talks to an API gateway; behind the gateway there are an order service, a payment service and a catalog service; the order service writes to an orders database and puts messages on a queue that a shipping worker reads; the catalog has its own database and a cache in front of it. Use one section for the front end and one for the back end.

A process for approving purchase orders: a request starts the process, a manager reviews it, a decision checks whether the amount is above a limit; above the limit the finance team reviews it too; then the order is approved or rejected and the requester is notified; the process ends.
An office network: an internet cloud, a firewall, a router, three switches, and on each switch a few computers; a printer and a file server on the first switch; a wireless access point on the second.
An organisation chart of a company of about twelve people: a director at the top, three department heads below her (engineering, sales, operations), and two or three people under each head.

A data pipeline: events come from mobile apps and from a website into an ingest service, are stored raw in object storage, cleaned by a batch job every night, loaded into a warehouse, and shown on two dashboards; a monitoring service watches the ingest service and the batch job.

A continuous delivery pipeline: a developer pushes code to a repository, a build server compiles and tests it, a failed build notifies the developer, a successful build produces an image stored in a registry, which is deployed first to a staging environment and, after a manual approval, to production.

A picture of a library described in words: a long desk near the entrance with a librarian behind it, three rows of shelves to the right, a reading table with four chairs in the middle, a window on the left wall and a clock above the desk.

A customer support desk: tickets arrive by email, chat and phone into a ticketing system; first-line agents answer simple tickets; complex tickets are escalated to specialists; a knowledge base is used by both; a weekly report is produced from the ticketing system.

The states of an online order: created, paid, packed, shipped, delivered, and cancelled; an order can be cancelled from created or paid; delivered is final; show the states and the transitions between them.

A smart home: a hub in the middle connected to lights in three rooms, a thermostat, a door lock and two cameras; a phone app talks to the hub through a cloud service; the cameras also store video in the cloud.
